description: The bar chart illustrates the Shapley values for different linguistic features across three multilingual models—mBERT, XLM-R, and chLSTM—as evaluated in the context of morphosyntactic probing. The horizontal axis categorizes linguistic features labeled L₄⁺, L₃, L₂, L₁, T, R₁, R₂, R₃, and R₄⁺, likely representing varying levels or types of morphosyntactic information, possibly ordered by complexity or position in a linguistic hierarchy. The vertical axis represents the Shapley value, ranging from 0 to 80, with tick marks at intervals of 20, indicating the relative contribution of each feature to model performance. Each group of three bars per category corresponds to one of the three models, with mBERT shown in light gray, XLM-R in dark gray, and chLSTM in olive green, as indicated by the legend in the upper right. The T (target) category shows the highest Shapley values across all models, with chLSTM reaching approximately 80, XLM-R around 55, and mBERT near 60. In contrast, L₃, R₃, and R₄⁺ show near-zero contributions for all models. L₁ and R₁ exhibit moderate values, with chLSTM and XLM-R performing similarly, while mBERT lags slightly. The chart suggests that the T feature is most influential for all models, and chLSTM generally assigns higher Shapley values than the other two, particularly for central features like T and L₁. The bars are not sorted by value but appear grouped by linguistic category, with no additional annotations or emphasis beyond color coding.
